title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-06-08
lineage: SBD > (MR - Set 1, MC - Set 2) > C >D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a monster 1969 show featuring a smoking Lovelight, Dancin' in the Streets opener, and a transcendent He Was A Friend Of Mine.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crisp, pure soundboard quality, making every nuance of the band audible. The performance itself is described as high‑energy and psychedelic, highlighted by an epic 27‑minute Lovelight with Wayne “The Harp” Ceballos, a blistering Dancin’ in the Streets opener, and a beautifully rendered He Was A Friend Of Mine, plus stellar jams on New Potato Caboose and China Cat Sunflower. Guest appearances by Elvin Bishop add extra color without detracting from the overall magic.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high 5‑star reviews praise both the musical performance and recording clarity; the few lower scores are outliers, so the combined show (70%) and recording (30%) weighting yields a near‑excellent rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple reviewers note the audio as crisp, pure and clear with no significant dropouts; the soundboard source captures the band’s dynamics very well.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend Of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: Powerful opener with Dancin', seamless transition into a soaring Lovelight, followed by tight jams and guest spots that keep the momentum high throughout both sets.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his vocal performance (including on Lovelight) and spectacular guitar solos; his interplay drives the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted as a psychedelic peak in Phil Lesh’s own book; bass solo in New Potato Caboose noted as superb.
